reasons: Classification is correct: the express warranty runs only sixty (60) days from the Effective Date with a hard December 31, 1999 cut-off, which is below the fallback of ninety (90) days for software and can expire on or before acceptance — a material duration failure, not a mere sub-element shortfall.

The redline is substantively targeted: only the duration phrase is replaced (twelve (12) months from acceptance under Section 3.1), while the media warranty, malicious-code warranty, remedy (correct/replace/terminate-and-refund) and exclusions are left intact, so the 0.754 changed-character ratio overstates the actual scope of the edit.
Defined term 'Warranty Period' is preserved in place, so downstream references in p0079 (media replacement, virus warranty) continue to operate.

Comment is accurate and on-tone: it states what changed, why (warranty could lapse before acceptance testing concludes), cites the 12-month preferred position and offers ninety (90) days from acceptance as the fallback, and confirms the remedy is unchanged.

Minor, non-disqualifying: the clause covers a hosted service as well as software and the single 12-month period is more than the 90-day services preference, but redlining to the preferred software period in a combined warranty is a reasonable, actionable ask.
